input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Explore: build a spatial autocorrelation tool (Moran's I, Geary's C, General G, LISA, Gi*, correlogram), verified against PySAL
errors: First reference run: Gi* z differed in sign from esda on a column with a negative sum; traced to esda dividing by sum(y), documented and tested rather than matched.
First calibration run showed the folded permutation p (esda/GeoDa convention) rejecting ~10% at 0.05; switched the engine to report the two-sided (doubled) p and kept the one-sided as p_sim_one.
FDR option could never flag anything with 999 permutations for 48 places (min p 0.002 > 0.05/48); engine now raises local permutations to 2n/alpha with a warning.
Permutation streams were seeded by column position, so one column gave different borderline clusters alone vs in the full table; now seeded by column name (tested).
Own test bugs (a line-wrapped phrase, commas inside calibration CSV labels) and a post front matter over the length limits, all fixed.

Local CI sweep: sibling-links failed (new tool had no sibling linking it; kriging-interpolation now links it, with a page test) and check_hidden_unicode flagged a literal U+FEFF in engine.mjs's BOM strip (now an escape). My own post edit mid-sweep voided the first sweep; voided workflows re-run clean.

doc_friction.issue: Census, BLS and USDA ERS hosts all 403 through the proxy; PyPI works, so data bundled inside a PyPI package (libpysal's us_income, BEA data) was the only route to real areal data. Worth adding to 'Outbound hosts' as a general fallback.
Finding an uncovered method took README and code greps; grep -w over READMEs missed instrumental-variables, which exists. A one-line-per-tool method index would be faster than the long table.

run_workflow_locally.py --for-changes takes ~20 min and voids itself if any tracked file changes; I edited the post (front-matter fix) mid-sweep and lost it. The warning is printed only at the end; printing it at the start would have saved a re-run.

deviations.why: Matching the reference implementation would mean esda's one-sided folded permutation p, which miscalibrates at 0.05.
deviations.did: Report the two-sided p by default, keep esda's value as p_sim_one, test the relationship and publish the calibration.
deviations.result: Two-sided permutation p rejects 3.8-6.1% under the null vs 9.1-12.0% for the folded p.

notes: Explore idea: spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I / LISA / Gi* hot spots) as a research-algorithm tool; 0 of 1,406 ventures mentioned Moran, Geary, Getis-Ord or LISA. Reference: esda 2.9.0 / libpysal 4.14.1, 9 cases, analytic numbers to 1e-9. Calibration (eval/calibration-output.txt, seeded, 1,000 null maps x 4 set-ups): folded permutation p 9.1-12.0% false positives at 0.05, doubled 3.8-6.1%; uncorrected LISA flags >=1 cluster on 88.7-99.0% of null maps, FDR 4.5-9.0%. Example: BEA state per-capita income 1929-2009 via libpysal's bundled example (proxy refused census/bls); Moran's I 0.667 (1934) -> 0.248 (1981) -> 0.429 (2009). Local checks: run_venture_tests.py spatial-autocorrelation 48/48 ok + site page checks ok; Chromium render desktop+phone, no console errors, no external requests, no horizontal scroll. GitHub showed 0 check runs on the PR (starved); verified locally with run_workflow_locally.py: sibling-links, ventures-tests, page-integrity, doc-refs, conflict-markers, duplicate-symbols, link-contrast, readme-live-links all pass on d280c9f; portfolio-validate 99/99 and pages.yml 6/6 passed in the first sweep; portfolio-pages' only failure was the orphan check, fixed (siblings.test.mjs 20/20).
